catalog_quote: Word-stress normally falls on the penultimate or antepenultimate syllable. Stress on final syllables is generally avoided in Sardinian. Indeed, a final epenthetic vowel is added to Latin monosyllables to yield paroxytonic forms. ... However, oxytonic forms do arise, mainly in Campidanese and Logudorese, as a result of elision of an intervocalic consonant: Log. /'pe/ (< pedem) 'foot', Camp. /dro'mi/ (< dOrmIre) 'to sleep'. A further process which yields final stress is truncation of the post-tonic sequence in vocative uses of nouns (particularly proper names and diminutives) and certain imperatives: /ju'a/ (<- /ju'anne/ 'John'), /pitsin'ne/ (<- /pitsin'neddu, -a/ 'little boy/ girl'), /a'ba/ (<- /a'barra/ 'stay'), /'te/ (<- /'tene/ 'hold'). When a verb (e.g. an imperative) is followed by a single clitic, the verb retains its normal stress pattern. However, if two or more clitics are added…

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is lexically fixed within the last three syllables, as in Italian: the vast majority of words are paroxytone (penultimate stress); antepenultimate and final stress exist and must be marked orthographically because they are not predictable from the word shape.
new_statements.exceptions: Words with final and antepenultimate stress exist as the marked minority (they get a graphic accent); example figiu ['fidʒu] 'son' is paroxytone.
new_statements.identity_note: Lai 2002 describes the Nuoro (Nuorese) dialect specifically (its lexical counts come from a Nuorese dictionary sample; fn. 162 says Contini's 1970a counts for Nughedu, Logudorese, are close). Vanrell et al. 2014 record Logudorese and Campidanese speakers but state the paroxytone generalization for Sardinian as a whole. Molinu 2021 speaks of 'le sarde' generally (her own fieldwork is Logudorese, Buddusò). Hofmann 1885 cites both Logudorese and Campidanese forms. None of the sources restricts the placement statement to a single village.

new_statements.quote: Il existe aussi une voyelle paragogique fixe [e] et plus rarement [i] / [o] qui, dans le dialecte de Nuoro, est placée après la voyelle finale des oxytons. Le développement de cette voyelle s'explique par l'hostilité des sardes à l'égard de l'oxytonie (p. 24) [...] M. L. Wagner (1984 [1941], § 13) avait déjà fait remarquer que le sarde est hostile aux oxytons. Dans les rares cas où ce type d'accent apparaît, une voyelle paragogique est toujours ajoutée en fin de mot (p. 85 fn. 234)
new_statements.translation: There is also a fixed paragogic vowel [e], more rarely [i]/[o], which in the Nuoro dialect is placed after the final vowel of oxytones. The development of this vowel is explained by the Sardinians' hostility to oxytony (p. 24) [...] M. L. Wagner (1984 [1941], § 13) had already remarked that Sardinian is hostile to oxytones. In the rare cases where this accent type appears, a paragogic vowel is always added at the end of the word (p. 85 fn. 234)

new_statements.relation_note: Nuoro (Nuorese) variety specifically. Compatible with Vanrell et al. 2014 and fills the empty catalog rule with quantified placement: penultimate default, lexical antepenultimate, final stress marginal and repaired.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is lexical (Romance type), overwhelmingly penultimate: table A on p. 52, counted over a 4000-entry Nuorese dictionary sample, gives paroxytones 21% (2-syll.) + 31% (3-syll.) + 28% (4-syll.) + 7% (5-syll.) + 1% (6-syll.) + 0.03% (7-syll.), i.e. about 88%; proparoxytones 7.5% + 4% + 0.6% + 0.2%, about 12%; oxytones 0.1% (monosyllables) + 0.03% (trisyllables); pre-proparoxytones 0.03%. Final stress is essentially banned: the few oxytones (ki, tu, da, kaffe..) receive a paragogic vowel ([kie], [tue], [dae]) so that the word surfaces as paroxytone.

new_statements.quote: De même, s'il existe en sarde une contrainte sur l'oxytonèse qui est respectée par ailleurs38, pourquoi ces formes ne sont pas réparées via l'épenthèse vocalique ? [fn. 38:] Comme le montre la réparation, via épenthèse, des formes oytones et subminimales ki >kie, mi > mie, tu > tue, etc. (Molinu 1999a[A]). (p. 55) [...] En effet, le mot minimal, en sarde, est constitué d'un trochée dissyllabique et cette contrainte est transgressée par les impératifs, les vocatifs et les interjections. (p. 56) [...] le pattern accentuel (oxytonie), des fausses paires minimales ([an'tɔ] (< [an'tɔna]) « Anto(nia)! » vs [an'to] (< [an'toni]) « Anto(ine)! ») (p. 56)
new_statements.translation: Likewise, if in Sardinian there is a constraint against oxytony that is otherwise respected [fn. 38: as shown by the repair, through epenthesis, of oxytone and subminimal forms ki > kie, mi > mie, tu > tue, etc. (Molinu 1999a)], why are these forms not repaired by vowel epenthesis? [...] Indeed the minimal word in Sardinian consists of a disyllabic trochee, and this constraint is violated by imperatives, vocatives and interjections. [...] the accentual pattern (oxytony), the false minimal pairs ([an'tɔ] (< [an'tɔna]) 'Anto(nia)!' vs [an'to] (< [an'toni]) 'Anto(ine)!')

new_statements.relation_note: Adds the constraint-based statement (no final stress; disyllabic trochee minimal word) and the systematic exception classes; consistent with Lai 2002 and Vanrell et al. 2014. Molinu's own data are Logudorese (Buddusò) and Sardinian generally.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Sardinian has a constraint against final (oxytone) stress that is normally enforced by vowel epenthesis (ki > kie, tu > tue), and a minimal-word requirement of a disyllabic trochee, i.e. the unmarked word ends in a stressed-unstressed sequence (penultimate stress). Where stress falls among the last syllables is otherwise lexical.
new_statements.exceptions: Truncated imperatives (na' < nara 'say!', le' < lea 'take!', mi < mira 'look!'), vocatives (oxytonic truncations [an'tɔ], [an'to]) and interjections violate both the anti-oxytone constraint and the minimal-word trochee; they sit at the periphery of the system.

new_statements.translation: A. Stress. In the following points the stress deviates from Latin: 1) The infinitives of the Latin 2nd conjugation, as in Catalan and by analogy with the infinitives of the Latin 3rd conjugation, throw the accent from the ending onto the stem syllable, without exception. [...] 2) Sardinian follows the general Romance tendency of placing the accent, in the 1st and 2nd plural present of the Latin 3rd conjugation, on the penultimate inflectional syllable. [...] 3) Some proparoxytones of the Latin 1st conjugation have in the singular present the Spanish accent, i.e. they become paroxytones: toleras, continuat, consideras, Logudorese and Campidanese. (Items 4-5 add stress retraction by one syllable in the 1st/2nd pl. imperfect subjunctive, Campidanese and Logudorese.)

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation and all auxiliary snippets (pp. 316, 326-327, 333) are present verbatim at the stated places in the held archive.org scanned text of Jones 1988; the second reader's independent confirmation stands. (2) Deciding source: a 1988 handbook grammar sketch by a Sardinian specialist, explicitly describing Logudorese-Nuorese (Lula), so languoid identity is correct; it is reputable but not the fullest or most recent phonological description (Molinu 2017, Contini 1987, Pittau 1972, Corda 1994, Mensching & Remberger 2016 exist; none held, none open). (3) Open sources downloaded now — Lai 2002 (instrumental thesis on Nuoro prosody, HAL), Molinu 2021 (HDR synthesis, HAL), Vanrell et al. 2014 (Loquens, OA), Hofmann 1885 (archive.org) — all either confirm or are silent: stress type is a lexical property within the last three syllables, paroxytones dominate (Lai's lexicon counts)

sources.quote: Synthesis of Molinu's work on (mainly Logudorese, Buddusò) Sardinian phonology. States a constraint against oxytony in Sardinian, repaired by vowel epenthesis (ki > kie, mi > mie, tu > tue; fn. 38), a disyllabic-trochee minimal word, and that truncated monosyllabic imperatives (mi' < mira, na' < nara, te' < tene) and truncated vocatives ([an'tɔ] < [an'tɔna]) are oxytone forms at the periphery of the system that escape repair. No general stress-placement algorithm is given; stress position is treated as lexical (proparoxytone vs paroxytone verb types discussed pp. 80-82).
